mapProfile.cameraFraming: Keep the complete storm-fallen oak and root seam, both formation glades, and all three reconnecting approaches readable in the production isometric camera.

styleAuthority.usage: Use the image for Heartlands color, material, storm-fallen oak scale, and pastoral woodland hierarchy; derive gameplay topology from this semantic contract.

composition.summary: An irregular Heartlands forest hollow organized around an enormous storm-fallen ancient oak and exposed root mass spanning a shallow diagonal dry ravine, with a broad southwest clover glade, smaller northeast fern-and-hazel glade, northwest fieldstone terrace, and southeast hawthorn loop.
visualHierarchy: The enormous storm-fallen ancient oak, shattered trunk, and exposed root mass dominate the central diagonal dry ravine without dividing the map into disconnected halves.
A broad sunlit clover glade in the southwest provides the principal open formation ground.
A smaller fern-and-hazel glade in the northeast provides a sheltered opposing formation ground.
A low northwest fieldstone terrace and a southeast hawthorn loop frame two outer reconnecting approaches.
Ancient oak, hazel, hawthorn, fern banks, roots, and rounded fieldstone shape an organic forest-owned boundary.
focalAreas: storm-fallen ancient oak and exposed root mass
broad southwest sunlit clover formation glade
northwest low fieldstone terrace and lookout
negativeSpace: Keep broad irregular breathing room inside the southwest clover glade and smaller northeast fern-and-hazel glade for readable formations.
Preserve navigable gaps around and beneath the fallen trunk and exposed root seam so the landmark never becomes a single choke.
Keep the northwest terrace and southeast hawthorn loop visually open enough to read as distinct reconnecting approaches.
Do not turn the dry ravine into water or a straight cleared strip.
density: Open sunlit clover and warm meadow grass across the broad southwest glade.
Moderate ferns, hazel stools, leaf litter, and dappled shade around the smaller northeast glade.
Dense ancient oak, hazel, hawthorn, root, and fern masses along the irregular outer forest edge.
Sparse rounded fieldstone on the low northwest terrace and at a few gentle level transitions.

areas.description: An enormous storm-fallen ancient oak and exposed root mass spanning the shallow diagonal dry ravine, with broad navigable passages around and beneath it.
A broad irregular sunlit clover formation glade with distinct entries into the central, northwest, and southeast approaches.
A smaller sheltered formation glade edged by ferns and hazel, with distinct entries from the oak seam, northwest terrace, and southeast loop.
A broad low fieldstone terrace and lookout reached by gentle slopes and a few fieldstone stairs, never an isolated peak.
A curving low route enclosed by irregular hawthorn clusters that reconnects both glades around the southeast side.

relationships.kind: paired curved entries into broad passages around and beneath the fallen trunk and exposed roots
reconnecting curved exits from both sides of the shallow dry ravine seam
curved northwest ascent by gentle forest slopes with a few fieldstone stairs
descending northwest terrace route that reconnects beyond the fallen oak
curved southeast departure between irregular hawthorn clusters
reconnecting southeast loop approach by gentle fern-edged slopes
secondary root-edged branch that prevents the northwest route from becoming a corridor
secondary ravine-edge branch that prevents the southeast route from becoming a corridor

connections: Use multiple broad gentle grassy, loamy, and fern-edged slopes for most level changes.
Use only a few low fieldstone stairs where the northwest terrace meets its curved approaches.
Keep the dry ravine shallow and crossable around several sides of the fallen trunk and root mass.
Keep every rise broad and connected; do not create an isolated peak or cliff-bound pad.

primaryApproaches: Provide exactly three broad tactical route families between the formation glades: around or beneath the fallen trunk and root seam, through the northwest fieldstone terrace, and around the southeast hawthorn loop.
Make all three curved approaches reconnect into one network at multiple points so no landmark, stair, or ravine crossing becomes a single choke.
Bend routes around the ancient oak, exposed roots, hazel stools, hawthorn, fern banks, and fieldstone instead of forming straight corridors.
secondaryApproaches: Branch the central oak-seam approach toward both outer routes before they enter the formation glades.
Use multiple gentle slopes and only a few fieldstone stairs to keep elevation choices broad and readable.
Preserve more than one navigable passage around or beneath the fallen trunk and exposed root mass.

boundaryIntent.description: Organic oak, hazel, fern, hawthorn, roots, fieldstone, and natural slopes own an uneven forest edge; never resolve the playable or rendered perimeter into a rectangle, grid, or continuous wall.

spawnIntent.formationCharacter: Opposing formations occupy the broad southwest sunlit clover glade and smaller northeast fern-and-hazel glade, each with local cover, maneuvering room, and access to all three reconnecting curved approaches.
forbiddenBehavior: Do not place candidates on detached pads.
Do not reserve full-height or full-width cleared spawn strips.
Do not mirror the two formation clearings or regularize them into matching shapes.
Do not make either formation depend on a single choke, stair, trunk passage, or ravine crossing.
Do not infer exact spawn coordinates by literally tracing the source image.

requiredLandmarks: enormous storm-fallen ancient oak and exposed root mass
broad southwest sunlit clover formation glade
northwest low fieldstone terrace and lookout
three reconnecting curved approaches around or beneath the oak seam and through both outer routes
multiple gentle slopes and a few fieldstone stairs
forbiddenPatterns: single-choke formations, routes, stairs, or ravine crossings
water, wet streambeds, ponds, or rivers
literal pixel, coordinate, or contour tracing

surfaces: sunlit Heartlands clover and warm meadow grass
dry ochre ravine loam and oak leaf litter
soft grassed and fern-edged natural slopes
connections: broad passages around and beneath the fallen trunk and root seam
a few rounded cream-gray fieldstone stairs
decorations: small rounded fieldstones and fallen twigs
